AlternateTargets: the bottom drops out of the bucket
Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'the bucket-bottom comes off' or 'the bottom drops out of the bucket.' The phrase occurs 109 times in 75 allowed texts. Its comparison form 'like the bucket-bottom falls out' (如桶底脫) occurs 38 times, including 26 exact endings in 'resembling the bucket-bottom falling out' (桶底脫相似). Xuefeng reports that after Deshan struck him, 'at that time I was as if the bucket-bottom had fallen out' (我當時如桶底脫相似); Yantou immediately challenges what Xuefeng brought in through the gate. Yuanwu uses the same comparison after 'under one phrase' (一言之下) and elsewhere joins the literal image to 'the mechanisms are exhausted' (桶底脫機關盡). The phrase is also recorded as a direct answer: asked 'What is buddha?' (如何是佛), Shoushan Huaizhi says, 'the bucket-bottom falls out' (桶底脫). A separate kitchen encounter uses the words literally: while noodles are cooking, the bucket-bottom suddenly falls out, the assembly cries that it is a pity, and the master says, 'the bucket-bottom falling out should itself be cause for joy—why are you distressed?' (桶底脫自合歡喜), before agreeing that the lost bucket of noodles is regrettable. The physical event and its simile therefore share one graph-level sense while appearing in an answer, recollection, comment, and kitchen exchange.
Senses.Note: The corpus does not provide a required direct-definition formula. It does provide a literal control case involving a noodle bucket, which prevents the comparison from being replaced by an imported abstraction. Xuefeng's report is preserved together with Yantou's objection rather than being treated as a standalone verdict.

Senses.Explanation: Literally 'right at this point' or 'on the spot' (當下: 當, 'at or right on,' plus 下, 'the point or spot'). In the corpus it is a temporal-locative adverb marking the juncture at which something happens, most often with a verb of sudden completion. Its counted collocations include 'awakened greatly on the spot' (當下大悟, 68 occurrences), 'right then knew where to return' (當下知歸, 46), and 'right then melted like ice' (當下冰消, 21). Related forms include 'right then received it' (當下領, 20), 'right then understood' (當下明, 12), 'right then rested' (當下休歇, 9), 'right then had no mind' (當下無心, 9), and 'right there it is' (當下便是, 4). Recorded examples say that Huike searched for mind without finding it and right then his mind was at ease (二祖搜心不可得，當下心安); that boundless bad actions and ignorance right then shattered like tiles and melted like ice (破無邊惡業無明當下瓦解氷銷); and that one takes it up on the spot (當下承當). The word names where the event lands in the account. It does not name a condition in which someone is told to remain.
Senses.Note: A corpus-wide adverb, not a master's private idiom. The corpus attaches it to sudden completions such as great awakening (大悟), knowing where to return (知歸), shattering and melting like ice (冰消瓦解), and the mind becoming at ease (心安). The collocation counts were verified across the 462-text Zen allowlist.

Occurrences.Kwic: 阿那箇是明上座本來面目。師當下大悟。徧體汗流。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Daoming of Mengshan in Yuanzhou (袁州蒙山道明禪師), also named Huiming or Senior Ming (慧明 / 明上座). Asked which is his original face (本來面目), Daoming awakens greatly on the spot (當下大悟) and sweats all over. This is narrative, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若於此會得，當下便是恩愛盡
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan (破山禪師語錄), first informal convocation (小參一). The phrase 'right there it is' (當下便是) introduces the stated consequence, showing a near-nominal deployment of the adverb.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, “at / meet the trigger or occasion.” In Chan records the occasion is repeatedly public and interpersonal: one account says that in all his questions and answers he “did not yield when meeting the occasion” (問答，當機不讓); a verse pairs a clear question and a direct answer with “meeting face-to-face on the occasion” (當機覿面). The phrase can introduce a request—“with one phrase meeting the occasion, please speak the teaching” (一句當機請師說法)—or appraise an immediate response. A master strikes the staff and says, “freed through on the occasion; it is no other thing” (當機透脫，更非別物). Yuanwu's verse says that buddhas and patriarchs “value what is ready-made when meeting the occasion” (佛祖當機貴見成) and immediately calls for someone to come before the assembly and settle doubt. Thus the corpus bends a general word for apt timing toward the live occasion of encounter, question, answer, and response.
Senses.Note: The graph for “trigger / occasion” (機) names the occasion being met in this compound.

Occurrences.Kwic: 凡與悟問答，當機不讓。

Occurrences.Kwic: 一句當機請師說法師云莫妄想
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk asks for one phrase meeting the occasion; the master answers, “do not think falsely.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 以拄杖卓一卓，「當機透脫，更非別物。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A staff strike accompanies the appraisal “freed through on the occasion.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 驚群敵勝乃英靈。佛祖當機貴見成。幸遇通人為證據。何妨出眾決疑情。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu's teaching-seat verse links meeting the occasion with coming before the assembly to resolve doubt.

Occurrences.Kwic: 通身是眼，覿面當機。電卷星馳，如何湊泊？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Face-to-face meeting of the occasion in a teaching-seat address.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, at the very place concerned. The expression occurs 846 times in 230 allowlisted texts. Chan records repeatedly couple it with results said to occur without going elsewhere: liberation 'right where it is,' arising right there and appearing wherever one goes, quiescence right there, and the place of teaching right there. In public exchanges it also retains its direct locative force: when a visitor quotes 'without leaving the very place, constantly clear,' a master is asked where that is. Another discourse asks how one recognizes the buddhas and immediately surpasses them right there. These predicates and questions load an ordinary locative expression within Chan discourse.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide locative sense. 'Right where it is' covers both physical and discourse-level complements; the evidence does not establish two different referents.

AlternateTargets: to let it pass right before one's face
to miss what is directly before one
Senses.Explanation: Literally, something is missed or allowed to pass while directly facing it. The phrase occurs as a verdict, a warning, and an author's acknowledgment. Meixi Du pairs two kinds of people: those who stand out shoulder it directly, while those confused about the head and recognizing a shadow miss it face-to-face (超群拔萃的，直下荷擔；迷頭認影的，當面錯過). In a letter he says that on first meeting a correspondent he did not recognize the correspondent's freedom and literary quality, “truly what is called missing it face-to-face” (誠所謂當面錯過也); this is the corpus's only formula using “what is called” for the term. Boshan Wuyi says, after asking whether anyone can assess the value of what he has presented, “one still must not miss it face-to-face” (也不可當面錯過). Elsewhere Boshan lists “rice is made from grain, soup is made from water, and a nun is made as a woman,” then says “do not miss it face-to-face” (飯是米做底、湯是水做底、師姑是女人做底，切莫當面錯過). Yunxi's record places the warning after “kites fly and fish leap; mountains stand and water flows” (鳶飛魚躍，山峙水流，切莫當面錯過). Panlong calls on his staff to bring news to the assembly, warns them not to miss it face-to-face, raises the staff, and asks whether they understand. The exact phrase occurs 134 times in 67 allowlisted files.
Senses.Note: The close variant “to miss it directly face-to-face” (當面蹉過) occurs 158 times in 65 files. “To miss it right before one” (覿面錯過) occurs 12 times in 11 files, and “to miss it before the eyes” (眼前錯過) occurs three times in three files. The entry translates the observable spatial and verbal shape; it does not supply an object where the text leaves that object unstated.

Occurrences.Kwic: 超群拔萃的，直下荷擔；迷頭認影的，當面錯過。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Meixi Du's address gives the paired verdict: “Those who stand out and rise above shoulder it directly; those confused about the head and recognizing a shadow miss it face-to-face.” Meixi is not in the roster.
